questions.q: What is the key difference between UNION and UNION ALL?
options: UNION ALL only works with numeric columns
UNION removes duplicate rows from the combined result; UNION ALL keeps all rows, including duplicates
UNION is faster than UNION ALL in every case
There is no difference between them
questions.explain: UNION performs duplicate removal on the combined result set, while UNION ALL simply concatenates both results without deduplication.

questions.q: What does Oracle call the set-difference operator that other databases like SQL Server call EXCEPT?
options: SUBTRACT
DIFF
MINUS
REMOVE
questions.explain: Oracle has traditionally called this operator MINUS; EXCEPT was added as a newer alias only in Oracle 21c.

options: Rows that appear in both query_A and query_B
Rows from query_B that do NOT appear in query_A
Every row from both queries combined
Rows from query_A that do NOT appear in query_B
questions.explain: MINUS (Oracle's set difference operator) returns rows present in the first query but absent from the second.

questions.q: What does INTERSECT return when comparing two supplier lists (invoiced in 2026, invoiced before 2026)?
options: Suppliers that appear in BOTH lists — invoiced both before and during 2026
Suppliers that invoiced in 2026 only
Suppliers that invoiced before 2026 only
Every supplier in the entire database
questions.explain: INTERSECT returns only the rows that appear in both result sets being compared.

questions.q: Why should you generally prefer UNION ALL over UNION when you know the two result sets cannot contain duplicate rows between them?
options: UNION ALL is always more accurate
UNION ALL automatically sorts the result, which UNION does not
UNION ALL skips the duplicate-removal step, making it faster with no downside if duplicates aren't a concern
There is no reason to prefer one over the other, ever
questions.explain: Since UNION's duplicate removal step has a cost, UNION ALL is preferable whenever you don't need (or know you won't have) duplicates to remove.
